criteria.blocker: Three of the nine named clauses fail at head. The remediation commit repaired a great deal here -- authorization and idempotent consumers genuinely moved from PARTIAL/BROKEN to holding, and five real-database workflow specs now exist where the prior audit had none -- but bounded reads still carry a full database transaction per row, two thirds of the accounting screens still render a failed read as an empty one, and one of the five new workflow specs fails at head.
criteria.clauses_failing: bounded indexed reads; frontend states; production-shaped workflow tests. Clauses 'immutable tenant-safe ledgers', 'normalized expenses and reconciliation', 'queue-backed exports/reminders', 'idempotent consumers', 'retention' and 'authorization' hold, each with a residual recorded below.
criteria.evidence:
FAILING CLAUSE 1 - bounded indexed reads. The INDEXED half is clean (`check:tenant-indexes` exit 0, 840 tenant tables / 840 leading-tenant indexes). The BOUNDED half is not. /Users/tarunchintakunta/Personal/streamline/streamlineos-backend/src/modules/finance/ap/payment-run-executor.service.ts:94 opens `for (const item of pendingItems) {` and :122 inside it does `await this.db.transaction(async (tx) => {` -- one full database transaction per payment-run item, unchanged at head. Six more N+1 growing loops remain in scope (accounting/gl/recurring-journals.service.ts, finance/ap/bills-due-check.service.ts, finance/tax/tax-compliance.service.ts, invoices/invoices-lifecycle.service.ts, invoices/invoices-payment.service.ts, invoices/invoices-write.service.ts). `check:n1-growing-loops` exits 0 over all seven because it is a RATCHET against a recorded count, not a prohibition -- a green gate is not evidence here. On the frontend, /Users/tarunchintakunta/Personal/streamline/streamlineos-frontend/frontend/features/accounting/vendors/vendors-list-page.tsx:77-81 requests `{ limit: 100 }` and :83 reads `query.data?.data ?? []` with no cursor follow-up, so a tenant with more than 100 outstanding vendors silently sees 100.

FAILING CLAUSE 2 - frontend states. Measured at head over features/accounting/**.tsx (excluding tests): 96 components read a query result AND render a loading branch; 64 of them contain no `isError` anywhere. Verified one end to end: features/accounting/vendors/vendors-list-page.tsx owns its own read (`useVendorsOutstanding` at :77), takes `items = query.data?.data ?? []` at :83, and passes `isLoading={query.isLoading}` plus an `emptyState` to DataTable at :124-126 -- so a failed or 403 read renders as 'no vendors', indistinguishable from an empty ledger. Two more confirmed: features/accounting/settings/setup-wizard-steps.tsx:62 and :155 (`const settings = settingsQuery.data;` -- a failed useAccountingSettings renders a blank currency/fiscal-year form the user can submit), and features/accounting/planning/revisions-sheet.tsx:41 (a failed members read renders raw UUIDs). Note the prior audit's F9 list of 27 named components DOES largely reproduce as fixed -- 21 gained a real error branch and 6 were miscategorised -- so this clause fails on the wider population, not on the audit's list.

FAILING CLAUSE 3 - production-shaped workflow tests. This is a real improvement over the prior audit's 'NOT MEASURED': five database-backed specs now exist and target the audit's own findings (accounting/core/__tests__/base-currency-statements.db.spec.ts, finance/ap/__tests__/payment-run-settled-amount.db.spec.ts, finance/controls/__tests__/provider-bridge-posting.db.spec.ts, invoices/__tests__/invoice-edit-gst-integrity.db.spec.ts, invoices/__tests__/invoice-numbering.db.spec.ts). But one of the five FAILS at head, and the cause is verified at source: /Users/tarunchintakunta/Personal/streamline/streamlineos-backend/src/modules/accounting/core/__tests__/base-currency-statements.db.spec.ts:198 ends beforeAll with `}, 90_000);` while :200 opens `afterAll(async () => {` with NO timeout, and its body runs `DELETE FROM organizations WHERE id = ${ORG_ID}` -- a repo-wide cascade -- under jest's default 5,000 ms hook limit. All 8 of its tests pass and then the suite fails on 'Exceeded timeout of 5000 ms for a hook', leaking its fixture rows. The same untimed-afterAll shape is in all five specs; the other four pass only because their cascades are smaller. Separately, all five are env-gated (`describeDb = ENABLED ? describe : describe.skip`, e.g. invoice-edit-gst-integrity.db.spec.ts:46 needs INV_DB_TESTS=1) so they are SKIPPED in an ordinary jest sweep -- I saw exactly that: `npx jest --runInBand --testPathPattern="modules/(billing|invoices)/"` reported 56 passed / 2 SKIPPED and 619 passed / 17 SKIPPED, exit 0. A skip is never a pass.

NAMED FACT VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY - assertBalanced IS on the posting path and IS exact. /Users/tarunchintakunta/Personal/streamline/streamlineos-backend/src/modules/accounting/posting/journal-posting.service.ts:92 `this.assertBalanced(draft.lines);` is the FIRST statement of persistJournalEntry, before the replay lookup and before any insert; the method at :73-88 sums through `sumDecimals`/`compareDecimals`, which are BigInt-scaled at scale 4 (src/modules/accounting/core/money.util.ts:80-86, :136-140), and it pins each line with `decimalFromNumber(l.debit)` -- the identical call used at the insert -- so it asserts over the exact bytes that get persisted. All four internal callers (:193, :215, :245, :267) route through it, and `git log -3 -- journal-posting.service.ts` shows the remediation commit never touched the file. Call-graph traced: five sites repo-wide INSERT into journal_lines, four carry a runtime balance assertion (journal-posting.service.ts:169 via :92; finance-posting.service.ts:231 via assertDebitsEqualsCredits at :125 plus finance-posting-lines.ts:78; recurring-journals.service.ts:348 and :390 via validateLines). The one exception is the reversal insert at finance-posting.service.ts:406, balanced by construction from rows already asserted. So reports/10-audit.md F3 ('P0 -- persistJournalEntry writes POSTED entries with no balance assertion at any layer') is REFUTED, and the release commit's rejection of it was correct.

A SECOND CLAIM I TESTED AND FOUND UNTRUE. The prior audit's F7 lists five accounting permissions as 'catalogued and grantable but bound to no route', among them accounting:access:view and accounting:access:manage. Those two are NOT unbound: they are generated for every module at src/modules/rbac/permissions/module-access.ts:9,15 (`name: \`${moduleKey}:access:view\``) and enforced dynamically at src/modules/module-access/module-access.helpers.ts:99 `resolved.get(\`${moduleKey}:access:${action}\`)` behind `@AuthorizedInService("assertModuleAccessPolicy")` on module-access.controller.ts:73 -- which is exactly why a literal grep of the backend source or of openapi.json finds zero. My own first grep made this mistake before I traced it. The other half of F7 was genuinely fixed: features/accounting/core/journal-entry-detail-page.tsx:57-59 now reads accounting:journal:create/:manage/:approve (with the old finding recorded in a comment at :54-55) and features/accounting/invoices/invoices-page.tsx:99 now reads accounting:manage, both with new permission-gates.test.tsx regression tests. So 'authorization' HOLDS; three grantable-but-unread catalog rows (accounting:journal:post, accounting:receivables:manage, accounting:receivables:approve) remain as hygiene.

RESIDUALS ON CLAUSES I AM SCORING AS HOLDING, recorded so they are not lost. (i) 'immutable tenant-safe ledgers' -- the reversal path builds its amounts through a JS double: src/modules/accounting/core/accounting-journal-entry.service.ts:205-206 `debit: Number(toDecimal(line.credit)), credit: Number(toDecimal(line.debit)),`. It round-trips exactly below 2^53/10^4 (about 900 billion at scale 4) and the entry still balances because both sides lose identically, so I am not scoring the clause on it -- but reversal is the ONLY correction path an immutable ledger has, so the failure mode is unrepairable. (ii) 'normalized expenses and reconciliation' -- src/modules/invoices/invoices-payment.service.ts:87 computes `remaining` from a `::float`-cast SQL sum and :92 admits `input.amount > remaining + 0.01`, so every invoice is overpayable by up to one paisa, and the locked re-check at :151-152 inherits the same tolerance with no comment justifying either. (iii) 'idempotent consumers' now HOLDS: the broken producer was finance/controls/fx.service.ts collapsing every settlement into one uniq_je_idempotency slot; at head :58-62 builds the key from `input.sourceType` plus `realized_gain_loss:${input.settlementId}` and all three callers pass a distinct settlement id.
